With or without food (food may reduce GI upset/nausea)

Not adequately studied in severe renal impairment; monitor

summary: Deferiprone (Ferriprox) is an oral iron chelator approved for transfusional iron overload in patients with thalassemia syndromes, sickle cell disease and other anemias. It binds iron in a 3:1 (drug:iron) complex that is excreted in the urine, often producing harmless reddish-brown urine discoloration. It carries a boxed warning for agranulocytosis/neutropenia that can lead to serious and fatal infections, so the absolute neutrophil count (ANC) must be measured before starting and weekly thereafter, with therapy interrupted if neutropenia or infection develops. Immediate-release tablets/oral solution are given as 75 mg/kg/day in three divided doses (up to a maximum of 99 mg/kg/day); extended-release tablets deliver the same total daily dose split into two doses. Other key risks include embryo-fetal toxicity, GI effects, elevated liver enzymes (ALT) and zinc deficiency.
indications: Treatment of transfusional iron overload in adult and pediatric patients 3 years of age and older with thalassemia syndromes, sickle cell disease, or other anemias

dosage.n: May titrate to max 99 mg/kg/day; round to nearest half tablet or 2.5 mL

dosage.d: Same total mg/kg/day given divided twice daily
dosage.n: Total daily dose equals the immediate-release total; titrate up to max 99 mg/kg/day

dosage.c: Dose adjustment for serum ferritin response
dosage.d: Adjust within the 75-99 mg/kg/day range to body iron burden
dosage.n: Consider interrupting if serum ferritin consistently falls below 500 mcg/L
Do not give with other drugs that cause neutropenia/agranulocytosis

admin: Available as immediate-release tablets and oral solution (dosed three times daily) and as extended-release tablets (dosed twice daily)
Take with or without food; taking with food may lessen nausea and other GI upset
Swallow extended-release tablets whole; do not crush, break, or chew
Measure ANC before starting therapy and weekly while on treatment
Round the calculated dose to the nearest half tablet (or nearest 2.5 mL of oral solution)
moa: Deferiprone is a bidentate ligand that binds ferric iron in a 3:1 (deferiprone:iron) molar ratio, forming a stable, neutral chelation complex that is eliminated in the urine. By chelating excess iron accumulated from chronic transfusions, it reduces total body iron burden and protects tissues from iron-mediated injury.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to deferiprone or any component of the product
relative: Concomitant use of other drugs associated with neutropenia or agranulocytosis
Significant hepatic impairment (limited data; ALT elevations reported)
monitor: Absolute neutrophil count (ANC) before starting and weekly

preg: Deferiprone can cause embryo-fetal harm based on its mechanism and animal data. Avoid use in pregnancy. Females of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 6 months after the last dose. Iron chelation should generally not be given during pregnancy unless clearly necessary.
lact: There are no data on the presence of deferiprone in human milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in the breastfed infant, advise patients not to breastfeed during treatment and for approximately 14 days after the last dose.
renal: Deferiprone has not been adequately studied in patients with severe renal impairment; use with caution and monitor. The drug and its iron complex are eliminated renally.
hepatic: Deferiprone has not been adequately studied in patients with severe hepatic impairment; use with caution and monitor. Increased ALT/liver enzyme elevations have been reported - monitor liver enzymes and consider interrupting therapy if a persistent increase occurs.

major: Other drugs known to cause neutropenia or agranulocytosis (e.g., clozapine, certain antithyroid agents, some chemotherapy) - avoid co-administration; additive risk of severe neutropenia
moderate: Polyvalent cation products (aluminum-, iron-, or zinc-containing antacids and mineral supplements) - may bind deferiprone; separate dosing by a few hours
UGT substrates - deferiprone is glucuronidated; UGT inducers/inhibitors may alter exposure
minor: Vitamin C - may theoretically increase iron availability; use cautiously per clinician judgment
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; taking with food can reduce nausea and GI upset.
interactions.alcohol: No specific deferiprone-alcohol interaction is established, but limit alcohol because of the need to monitor liver enzymes.
interactions.diagnostics: Commonly causes harmless reddish-brown discoloration of the urine (chromaturia) from the iron-deferiprone complex; may elevate ALT and lower serum zinc.

serious: Agranulocytosis (severe neutropenia) leading to serious and fatal infections
rare: Increased intracranial pressure-type symptoms reported rarely
emergency: Fever, sore throat or other signs of infection (possible agranulocytosis - urgent ANC check)
Signs of liver injury (jaundice, dark urine, severe abdominal pain)

monitoring: Absolute neutrophil count (ANC): measure before starting and WEEKLY thereafter; interrupt for neutropenia or any infection
Serum ferritin and body iron burden to guide dosing
Signs and symptoms of infection at each visit
counsel: Report any signs of infection - fever, sore throat, flu-like symptoms - to your doctor right away; you will need weekly blood counts (ANC)
Your urine may turn reddish-brown - this is harmless and expected from the medicine binding iron
Take with or without food; taking with food may ease nausea, and swallow extended-release tablets whole
Tell your doctor about all other medicines, especially any that can lower white blood cells, and separate antacids or iron/zinc supplements by a few hours
If you can become pregnant, use effective contraception and do not breastfeed; tell your doctor if you are or may become pregnant
pk: Reduction in body iron over weeks to months of chelation therapy
Plasma peak ~1 hour after a dose (delayed by food)
Immediate-release dosed three times daily; extended-release twice daily
Store at 20-25 C (excursions 15-30 C permitted); keep tightly closed, protect from moisture
pearls: Boxed warning: agranulocytosis/neutropenia can lead to serious and fatal infections - measure ANC before starting and WEEKLY thereafter, and interrupt for neutropenia or infection
Advise patients to report any signs of infection (fever, sore throat) immediately
Harmless reddish-brown urine discoloration (chromaturia) is expected from the iron-deferiprone complex
Avoid combining with other agents that cause neutropenia/agranulocytosis; separate polyvalent cation antacids and Fe/Zn supplements by a few hours
Monitor ALT and serum zinc; embryo-fetal toxicity means effective contraception is required
Same total mg/kg/day applies whether using immediate-release (TID) or extended-release (BID) formulations
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is almost time for the next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose - do not double up. Resume the regular schedule.
overdose: No acute overdose syndrome is well characterized. In the event of overdose, monitor closely for neutropenia/agranulocytosis, GI effects and neurologic symptoms, obtain an ANC, and provide supportive care. There is no specific antidote.
